description: Welcome to Team Martians! We are building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed to inspire and prepare the next generation of space explorers. Using real NASA data and engaging game mechanics, we’re turning complex astronaut training and Mars mission prep into a fun, hands-on adventure for kids.
summary:
THE MARTIANS: Build. Survive. Explore. Discover. is an interactive 2D Mars survival and colony-building game designed to make space science exciting for children.

Players become Mars colony operators responsible for developing a settlement. They explore different areas, complete missions, collect minerals, manage resources, repair equipment, earn Mars credits, unlock rooms, and purchase upgrades. Activities include mining, communication, power management, greenhouse maintenance, research, and engineering mini-games. Random events like dust storms and generator failures challenge players to think and solve problems.

The game addresses the challenge by turning the difficulties of Mars colonization into simple, interactive learning experiences. It introduces children to space exploration, engineering, scientific research, and resource management.

We developed it using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code and a web browser.

Its creativity comes from combining colony building, exploration, trading, upgrades, and educational missions. We considered children's age, simple controls, accessibility, engaging visuals, and educational value.

Our goal is to inspire young learners to become curious about science, technology, engineering, and the future of space exploration.
details:
THE MARTIANS: Build. Survive. Explore. Discover.

Project Description

The Martians is an interactive, 2D Mars survival and colony-building game designed to introduce children to the challenges of living on Mars through fun, exploration, and problem-solving.

Players take on the role of a Mars colony operator and are responsible for maintaining and expanding a Martian base. They explore different sections of the colony, complete missions, collect minerals, repair equipment, manage resources, and earn Mars credits to unlock rooms and purchase upgrades.

The game includes different interactive activities inspired by real space exploration challenges, such as operating communication systems, mining minerals, managing power, maintaining a greenhouse, and completing engineering mini-games. Random events such as dust storms and generator failures add challenges that encourage players to think and make decisions.

Benefits of the Project

  • Makes space science and Mars exploration engaging and accessible to children.
  • Introduces basic concepts of engineering, resource management, and scientific research.
  • Encourages logical thinking, creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving.
  • Helps children understand the difficulties astronauts may face while establishing a human settlement on Mars.
  • Combines learning with interactive gameplay rather than relying only on theoretical information.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to inspire young learners to become curious about space science, technology, engineering, and exploration. The Martians transforms complex concepts of Mars colonization into simple, enjoyable missions. It aims to encourage children to think like scientists, engineers, and future space explorers.

Tools, Technologies, and Software Used

  • HTML5 – Game structure and interface.
  • CSS3 – Visual design, animations, and game layout.
  • JavaScript – Game logic, interactive missions, resource management, events, and controls.
  • Visual Studio Code – Code development and editing.
  • Web browser – Running and testing the game.

Creativity and Innovation

The Martians turns the idea of surviving on Mars into an interactive colony-management experience. Instead of simply reading about Mars, players actively participate in building and maintaining a settlement. Features such as mining, trading, room upgrades, timed missions, random emergencies, and engineering mini-games make the learning experience engaging and replayable.

Factors Considered During Development

We considered the target audience, especially children and beginners in space science. The game was designed with simple controls, an easy-to-understand interface, colourful 2D graphics, progressive challenges, and interactive learning activities. We also considered the importance of making Mars survival concepts understandable while keeping the gameplay enjoyable and accessible on an ordinary computer.

The Martians is more than a game: it is a small step toward inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
